question.leadin: A meeting in this city was interrupted by Napoleon's escape from Elba.
question.text: Name this host of an 1815 meeting that established the balance of power of Europe in the 19th century, the capital of Austria.
question.clue: Many of this city's parks were built under its mayor Karl Lueger, whose anti-Semitic rhetoric likely inspired one-time resident Adolf Hitler.

swap.text: What nephew of Franz Josef was killed in that attack?
swap.answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand [or Francis Ferdinand; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.leadin: Genetic defects such as severe underbite and large chins recurred in this family due to inbreeding.
question.text: Name this central European noble family which included Maximilian I, Marie Antoinette, Charles V, and Maria Theresa.
question.clue: The founder of this house gained significant parcels of land after his victory at the Battle of Marchfeld, and the death of a later member of this house served as the extinction of its non-Styrian branch.

swap.leadin: German Chancellor Otto Von Bismarck's statement that a "great European war" would start from "some... foolish thing in the Balkans" predicted the assassination of this person.
swap.text: Name this Austrian Archduke who was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip in 1914, kicking off a series of events leading to the start of World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Franz Ferdinand [or Archduke Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria]
swap.clue: This Archduke of Austria, a nephew of Franz Joseph I.

question.leadin: This politician claimed that "when France sneezes, Europe catches a cold."
question.text: Name this Austrian Chancellor who was in power from 1821 until his ousting in the revolutions of 1848. As foreign minister this man presided over the conference at the end of the Napoleonic wars.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.leadin: In the 18th century, Austria was not exactly friendly to the idea of a female ruler.
swap.text: Name this Austrian ruler whose father Charles VI attempted to facilitate her ascension to the throne with the passage of the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.
swap.clue: To govern compulsory peasant labor, this monarch issued the Robot Patent.

question.leadin: This empire was founded in the 1867 Ausgleich ("OWSS-glykh") and was dissolved in the Treaties of Saint Germain and Trianon ("TREE-uh-non").
question.text: Name this empire that was first ruled by Franz Josef I.
question.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or Austro-Hungarian Empire or Österreichisch-Ungarische Monarchie or Osztrák-Magyar Monarchia; prompt on dual monarchy; do not accept “Austria” or “Hungary” alone]
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.leadin: This empire used "K.U.K." as its official abbreviation on ships and various articles of state in order to reflect political realities of split power.
swap.text: Name this European empire that was formed by a namesake 1867 compromise. It was one of the members of the pre-World War I Triple Alliance along with Italy and the German Empire.
swap.clue: The phrase "k.u.k" was used as a term for this country's system of government after the Ausgleich.

question.text: This author of Der Judenstaat opposed the Uganda Project and established the First Zionist Congress.
question.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

swap.leadin: After World War II, this event led to the formation of the "victim theory."
swap.text: Name this event translated as "connection" that Karl Schuschnigg failed to prevent. An original language term is required.
swap.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

question.leadin: This ruler's foreign minister was Prince Felix of Schwarzenberg.
question.text: Name this ruler whose son Crown Prince Rudolf committed suicide in the Mayerling Incident. A member of the League of Three Emperors, this man named his nephew, the husband of Countess Sophie, as his heir.
question.answerHtml: Franz Joseph I of Austria [or Francis Joseph I]
question.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the city of Pressburg.
swap.text: The War of the Third Coalition was ended by the 1805 Peace of Pressburg between Napoleon and this final Holy Roman Emperor. Along with Tsar Alexander I of Russia, this emperor was defeated at the Battle of Austerlitz.
swap.clue: Name that French monarch who had earlier challenged Charles in the election for Holy Roman Emperor.

question.text: Before Balfour, Joseph Chamberlain worked with this man to establish a temporary Jewish homeland in the Uganda Scheme. This founder of Zionism discussed the "Jewish Question" in his 1895 pamphlet Der Judenstaat ("dare YOO-den-shtaht").
question.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

swap.leadin: He issued an Edict of Toleration in 1782 extending political and religious rights to non-Catholics.
swap.text: Name this enlightened despot who also established a Universal Code of Civil Law in 1786.
swap.clue: This ruler sent generals Lacy and Laudon on a series of tactical maneuvers in one conflict that saw little actual fighting, the War of Bavarian Succession, and, in response to the peasants' revolt of Horea, abolished serfdom.

question.text: The Unholy Alliance resulted from its parties' mutual hatred of this family that ruled the Holy Roman Empire and Spain.
question.clue: Inbreeding devastated the genetics of this family, giving them a namesake "lip."

swap.text: This man served as secretary general from 1972 to 1981. He was elected president of Austria in 1986 despite revelations that he served as an interpreter and intelligence officer to a German unit in World War II that committed war crimes.
swap.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

question.leadin: Try to keep track of all those damn World War I treaties so you can answer this bonus.
question.text: Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Poland, and Yugoslavia were recognized by the newly formed Austria in this treaty, which shares its name with a 1570 treaty made during the French wars of religion.

swap.text: In the years leading up to World War I, the Austro-Hungarian military Chief of Staff was this bonehead, who got Austria to declare war on Serbia and then screwed up basically everything in the first half of the war.
swap.answerHtml: Franz Conrad von Hoetzendorf [or Franz Xaver Josef Conrad von Hoetzendorf; accept von Hoetzendorf]

question.text: This man replaced Metternich as Austria's chief minister, orchestrated the abdication of Ferdinand I, and attempted to restore the absolutist rule of the Hapsburgs as advisor to Franz Joseph I.

swap.text: The War of Austrian Succession was fought over the right of this monarch to ascend to the Austrian throne, which went against Salic Law and was supported by the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.
